notes.title: Google built its own lock. Then it called AMD.
body: Monday, the chip crowd limped back from a brutal week. AMD walked in with a fresh haircut and a story to tell. The stock closed up 13.26%, at $508.58. SOXX, a fund that holds a basket of chip stocks, rose 7.49%. Same session, nearly double the group’s bounce.

The story landed before the opening bell. AMD said its fifth-generation EPYC processors run the host side of Google Cloud’s new TPU 8tx. A TPU is Google’s own AI chip. The host CPU is the stage manager: it schedules the work, preps the data and keeps the TPUs fed. Google Cloud’s Mark Lohmeyer said the pairing brings hardware-enforced confidential computing to Cloud TPUs for the first time. In normal words, the data stays locked even while the machine is working on it. Model weights, prompts, the whole diary.

Plot twist. Google already makes its own server CPU. It’s called Axion, it’s Arm-based, and Google has run it alongside its recent TPUs so it leans less on outside chip vendors. So this is the homeowner who designed a custom lock, then handed the neighbor the spare key to the safe room. My read: when the job was security, Google decided the neighbor’s deadbolt was better. That’s a real compliment from a company that would love to need nobody.

Now rewind to Thursday. AMD fell 17.26% in one session, to $404.40, when the market dumped anything tied to AI data centers. Two sessions later, it closed 4.05% above Wednesday’s close. SOXX is still 2.25% under it. The rest of the class is icing its ankles. AMD is already running laps. Oppenheimer also upgraded the stock Monday, per Yahoo Finance’s recap, so the press release showed up with a hype man.

Here are the receipts I don’t have. Neither company put a dollar figure on this. No chip count. No price. No date for general availability, which is when any customer can actually rent the thing. This is a seating chart, not an invoice. A 13% day is a lot of applause for an announcement that hasn’t billed anyone yet.

I get the itch. The stock took a punch, got up swinging, and your thumb wants in like it’s a limited drop. The catch: buying after a 13% day means paying Monday’s price for news that may not show up in revenue for a while. And if Google’s next TPU quietly ships with Axion as the host, the chosen-one story gets a lot shorter. That’s what would prove the hype wrong.

One thing on my calendar: the day Google posts TPU 8tx pricing and a general-availability date. That’s when a press release turns into a bill. Until then, AMD has the spare key. I want to see who actually moves in.

performance.window: Nov. 9, 2026 · one session, close to close (Nov. 6 to Nov. 9)

notes.flowRemark: The options crowd was busy on the same day as the news, and some of it looked like people buying short-dated protection after the pop. I read that as a seatbelt for the ride home, not a verdict. I’m watching whether that insurance gets rolled out or quietly dropped this week.

notes.title: Nvidia ghosted the rally. The board has questions.
body: Monday’s market showed up to the party in sequins. Nvidia showed up in sunglasses, parked itself by the snack table and refused to dance. The index went green. The chip king went red. When the most popular kid skips the group photo, people start texting.

Here’s what we actually know. On Sunday, Nvidia’s board said it opened an independent investigation after reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. Same statement, same breath: the board has no reason to think company secrets or national security were compromised. That’s corporate for “we’re checking the locks, nothing looks missing, please stop ringing the doorbell.” Cute. I’ll stop ringing when I see what the locksmith finds.

Also, this was not Nvidia’s first bad night out this week. Stocks partied after the midterms. Then Thursday flipped the lights on at 2 a.m. The Nasdaq fell 5.5%. SOXX, a fund that holds a basket of chip stocks, fell 12.15%. The worry: after Democrats won, new data centers could catch more fights over permits and power bills. That’s a fear about future fights, not a new law. But a GPU can write your wedding toast in nine languages and still can’t get the zoning board to text back. No building, no rack. No rack, no delivery.

Plot twist the timeline missed: Nvidia actually held up better than its friends. Five sessions through Nov. 6, Nvidia fell 8.8%. The chip fund fell 13.13%. Not a trophy. Still a receipt. Thursday was the whole squad getting dragged out of the club together. Monday was Nvidia doing the walk of shame alone while everyone else went to brunch. That’s when the board story earns its own headline. The chart shows me the split. It can’t tell me how much is scandal and how much is leftover hangover.

Now, the dip. I see you. It’s down, it’s Nvidia, and your thumb is hovering over buy like it’s hovering over an ex’s new story at 1 a.m. Very human. Also how people end up apologizing over coffee. Before I touch it, I want one receipt. Customers pushing deliveries? Show me dates. Shipping on time but getting paid slower? Show me the cash. Other chip names sliding again? Then it’s a group-chat problem, not an Nvidia scandal.

Because there’s a canyon between a customer saying “take the chips in March instead” and an investor whispering “what if they take the chips in March instead?” One moves real revenue out of the quarter. The other just moves the stock, before a single order changes. If someone swears a delay is real, ask for the project name and the date. Rumors never bring those. Receipts always do.

Nvidia reports Nov. 17, and I’ll be in the front row. Two questions. What did the board find? And did any customer actually move a delivery date? Until then, the chart gets one browser tab and the receipts get another. Yes, I have too many tabs. These two pay rent.

performance.window: Five sessions through Nov. 6, 2026 · close to close

notes.flowRemark: Friday’s options bets were placed before the board said a word, so they’re yesterday’s gossip. I’m watching whether people keep paying up for crash insurance now that the headline is out.
